title: Background jobs process the same message twice
description: Fix duplicate background job execution caused by at-least-once delivery using idempotency, message deduplication, and the outbox pattern.

data.text: Your order confirmation emails are being sent twice. Your inventory is being decremented twice. The database shows two entries for the same background job ID. The message broker guarantees at-least-once delivery, which means duplicates are expected. You need to make your consumers idempotent and add safeguards to prevent duplicate processing from causing business harm.

items: The consumer acknowledges the message after processing, but the network drops the ACK, so the broker redelivers
The consumer crashes after processing but before acknowledging, and the message is redelivered on restart
The message broker replicates the message across partitions and delivers it twice during a leader election
A manual replay of the queue was performed without filtering already-processed IDs
The job queue does not enforce uniqueness on the message ID, allowing enqueue-time duplicates

terms.definition: A messaging guarantee that a message will be delivered one or more times, but never zero times.
The property that processing the same message multiple times produces the same result as processing it once.
A message that consistently causes a consumer to fail, often requiring manual intervention or dead-letter routing.
A holding queue for messages that cannot be processed successfully after all retry attempts.
Storing messages in the same database transaction as the business event, then publishing them reliably to a broker.

items: Store a record of processed message IDs in a durable table with a unique constraint
Before processing, check whether the message ID already exists in the processed table
Use database transactions to ensure the idempotency check and business operation are atomic
Set a TTL on processed message records to prevent the table from growing indefinitely
Return a 200 OK for redelivered messages even if the business result is unchanged

cards.title: Idempotency key table
cards.description: Insert a unique message ID before processing; skip if already present.

cards.title: Outbox pattern
cards.description: Write messages to an outbox table in the same transaction as the business event.

cards.title: Message deduplication in broker
cards.description: Use broker-native deduplication (e.g., AWS SQS FIFO, Azure Service Bus deduplication).

cards.title: Business-level idempotency
cards.description: Design the business operation itself to be safe to repeat (e.g., upserts, conditional updates).
cons: Not all operations are naturally idempotent

data.title: Idempotent consumer with a processed-message table
data.content: A background job processor that checks for duplicates before acting:

data.caption: Idempotent message processing flow with duplicate detection
data.definition:
graph TD
    A[Message received] --> B[Check processed table]
    B -->|Exists| C[Return 200 OK]
    B -->|Not found| D[Begin transaction]
    D --> E[Process business logic]
    E --> F[Insert processed message]
    F --> G{Transaction commits?}
    G -->|Yes| H[ACK message]
    G -->|No| I[Rollback, retry later]
    C --> H
    H --> J[Done]
    I --> K[Broker redelivers]
    K --> B

data.title: Do not rely on the broker for exactly-once semantics
data.text: Most message brokers offer at-least-once delivery. Even brokers with deduplication have a limited window and do not protect against application crashes between processing and acknowledgment.

data.title: Make a background job idempotent
data.description: Find a background job or message consumer in your codebase that does not currently handle duplicates. Add an idempotency check and a processed-message table.
steps: Identify a job that could cause harm if run twice (e.g., sending money, sending email)
Create a ProcessedMessages table with a unique MessageId column
Modify the consumer to check this table before processing
Wrap the check and business logic in a database transaction
Write a test that simulates a redelivered message and verifies the job is skipped
data.expectedOutcome: You should have a consumer that safely ignores duplicate messages without causing duplicate side effects.

data.title: Summary
points: At-least-once delivery is the norm; design for duplicates from day one
Use a unique constraint on processed message IDs to enforce idempotency at the database level
The outbox pattern couples message publishing to the business transaction for reliability
Test duplicate handling explicitly; do not assume it works
data.takeaway: Duplicate messages are not a bug in the broker; they are a property of distributed systems. Your job is to make them harmless.
